ultrasound.title: Distal phalanx of left index finger · ultrasound evidence & limits · draft
ultrasound.body: For an index, middle, ring or little finger, the distal phalanx begins beyond the distal interphalangeal joint. High-frequency ultrasound examples relate the terminal extensor tendon to the dorsal joint level and the deep flexor tendon to the distal-phalangeal base. These are distinct dorsal and volar soft-tissue windows. The selected source bone supplies a location cue for its base and terminal end, not either tendon’s actual insertion footprint or an acquired image.
bullets: Confirm the real finger and dorsal or volar side independently; model rotation is not probe orientation.
Neither a smooth atlas cortex nor a limited ultrasound window establishes marrow condition or excludes fracture.
ultrasound.note: Original educational draft; revision-bound radiologist review pending. This source surface is not an acoustic image, acquisition simulator, marrow study or fracture-exclusion test. No patient registration is supplied. Atlas, imaging-case and paid-lecture access remain independent.

pathology.title: Distal phalanx of left index finger · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Mallet injury disrupts the terminal extensor mechanism, sometimes with an avulsed bone fragment. It can therefore occur with or without a visible fracture.
bullets: Loss of active fingertip extension is a functional finding, not a diagnosis made from bone shape alone.
The distal phalanx and its DIP joint remain separate from the nail bed and terminal extensor tendon. No tendon discontinuity or fragment is modelled.
pathology.note: Draft teaching; independent anatomical and clinical review pending. Educational context, not a patient diagnosis or treatment plan.

clinical.title: Distal phalanx of left index finger · Clinical context · draft

bullets: No splinting schedule or operative threshold is inferred from this intact reference surface.

pathology.title: Left first common palmar digital artery · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Common digital arteries can have atypical origins and courses relative to finger flexor tendons. A 33-hand cadaver study found deeper variants supplying the second and fourth web spaces, illustrating why an unexpected vessel can be vulnerable during surgery.
bullets: A variant course is not an occlusion; neither its frequency nor its exact source-label counterpart is inferred here.
The source-numbered common branch remains distinct from a proper artery on a finger.

pathology.title: Right third common palmar digital artery · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Common digital arteries can have atypical origins and courses relative to finger flexor tendons. A 33-hand cadaver study found deeper variants supplying the second and fourth web spaces, illustrating why an unexpected vessel can be vulnerable during surgery.
bullets: A variant course is not an occlusion; neither its frequency nor its exact source-label counterpart is inferred here.
The source-numbered common branch remains distinct from a proper artery on a finger.

pathology.title: Left fourth common palmar digital artery · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Common digital arteries can have atypical origins and courses relative to finger flexor tendons. A 33-hand cadaver study found deeper variants supplying the second and fourth web spaces, illustrating why an unexpected vessel can be vulnerable during surgery.
bullets: A variant course is not an occlusion; neither its frequency nor its exact source-label counterpart is inferred here.
The source-numbered common branch remains distinct from a proper artery on a finger.

pathology.title: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of right middle finger · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: A finger wound can damage a digital artery together with nearby nerves. The effect on circulation depends on the remaining blood supply; an artery injury and a sensory deficit are related but separate clinical questions.
bullets: A small retrospective study compared one- and two-artery supply in selected well-perfused fingers.
Its findings are not a rule that an injured artery may always be left unrepaired or divided.
Ten represented proper arterial identities: six right and four left. Missing counterparts are not mirrored. Anatomical medial/lateral is a source label, not the current screen side.

pathology.title: Medial proper palmar digital artery of right index finger · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: A finger wound can damage a digital artery together with nearby nerves. The effect on circulation depends on the remaining blood supply; an artery injury and a sensory deficit are related but separate clinical questions.
bullets: A small retrospective study compared one- and two-artery supply in selected well-perfused fingers.

A combined cadaver and Doppler study, including eight living hands, distinguished compressible veins from gliding tendons. bullets: Use the skin, intervening fascial layers and deeper tendons as orientation landmarks. The small study supports these relationships, not a complete ultrasound map of every tributary or a fixed depth for every hand.

ultrasound.title: Dorsal venous network of left hand · Ultrasound orientation · draft
ultrasound.body: On dorsal-hand ultrasound, orient the superficial venous layer above the extensor tendons. A combined cadaver and Doppler study, including eight living hands, distinguished compressible veins from gliding tendons. Larger dorsal veins occupied an intermediate fatty layer, with the extensor tendons deeper.
bullets: Use the skin, intervening fascial layers and deeper tendons as orientation landmarks. The small study supports these relationships, not a complete ultrasound map of every tributary or a fixed depth for every hand.

Dorsal metacarpal vein patterns vary. The cited variation study used tourniquet enhancement or near-infrared illumination, not ultrasound; its patterns are anatomical context rather than proof of sonographic visibility.

This selection is one retained dorsal network per hand. Palmar arches and digital or metacarpal vein groups are separate source identities; the dorsal study does not validate their ultrasound appearance.

Compare the model with separation at zero. Its static surface cannot demonstrate compression, tendon motion, blood flow or patency, and supplies no patient registration, diagnostic conclusion or procedural route.

pathology.title: Dorsal venous network of left hand · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: A cannula or injection can be followed by inflammation of a superficial hand vein, causing tenderness, warmth and swelling. Such symptoms need assessment rather than being diagnosed from a visible dorsal-vein pattern.
bullets: Redness may be less obvious on darker skin; pain and swelling also matter.
A blue vein display cannot distinguish phlebitis, a clot, infection or fluid leakage.
